examples.en: The bottle's opening was narrow, so I used a funnel.

examples.ko: 기름을 부을 때는 깔때기가 있으면 편해요.
examples.en: It's easier when you have a funnel for pouring oil.

examples.ko: 깔때기 없이 부었더니 바닥에 다 흘렀어요.
examples.en: I poured it without a funnel and spilled it all over the floor.

examples.ko: 주방 서랍에서 작은 깔때기 좀 꺼내 주세요.
examples.en: Please take a small funnel out of the kitchen drawer.

examples.ko: 종이를 깔때기 모양으로 말아서 소금을 넣었어요.
examples.en: I rolled the paper into a funnel shape and poured in the salt.

examples.ko: 이 깔때기는 구멍이 작아서 물이 천천히 내려가요.
examples.en: This funnel has a small hole, so the water goes down slowly.

explain: 주방뿐 아니라 과학 실험이나 자동차에 기름을 넣을 때도 자주 나와요. 위는 넓고 아래는 좁은 모양을 말할 때 '깔때기 모양'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It appears not only in the kitchen but also in science experiments and when putting oil into a car. People also say '깔때기 모양' for anything wide at the top and narrow at the bottom.

examples.ko: 방에 있는 형광등이 아까부터 계속 깜빡거려요.
examples.en: The fluorescent light in the room has been flickering since a while ago.

examples.ko: 렌즈를 끼면 눈이 건조해서 눈을 자주 깜빡거려요.
examples.en: When I wear lenses my eyes get dry, so I blink often.
The cursor is blinking on the computer screen.

examples.ko: 배터리가 거의 없는지 불빛이 깜빡거리다가 꺼졌어요.
examples.en: The battery must have been almost empty; the light flickered and went out.

examples.ko: 신호등이 깜빡거릴 때는 길을 건너지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't cross the street when the traffic light is blinking.

examples.ko: 졸려서 눈이 깜빡거리는 걸 친구가 봤어요.
examples.en: My friend saw my eyes fluttering because I was sleepy.

explain: 불빛이 켜졌다 꺼졌다 할 때와 눈을 자꾸 감았다 뜰 때 둘 다 써요. '깜빡하다'는 '잊어버리다'라는 다른 뜻이니 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It is used both for lights going on and off and for eyes opening and closing repeatedly. Do not confuse it with '깜빡하다', which means to forget.

examples.en: The child looked at me, blinking.
Maybe dust got in; my eyes keep blinking.
He was so surprised that he could only blink.

examples.ko: 아기가 졸린 눈을 깜짝거리다가 잠이 들었어요.
examples.en: The baby blinked its sleepy eyes and then fell asleep.

examples.ko: 눈을 깜짝거리지 말고 가만히 있어 보세요.
examples.en: Try to stay still without blinking.
The way the puppy blinks its eyes is cute.

explain: 주로 눈에 쓰고, 불빛이 껐다 켜지는 것은 '깜빡거리다'가 더 자연스러워요. '깜짝 놀라다'의 '깜짝'과는 쓰임이 달라요.
explain_en: It is mainly used for eyes; for lights going on and off, '깜빡거리다' sounds more natural. It is used differently from the '깜짝' in '깜짝 놀라다'.

examples.en: A white rabbit hops around on the grass.
The child hopped over the puddle.
A small frog jumped up by the pond.

examples.ko: 동생이 기뻐서 방 안을 깡충깡충 돌아다녀요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is so happy, hopping around the room.

examples.ko: 유치원 아이들이 깡충깡충 뛰면서 노래를 불러요.
examples.en: The kindergarten kids sing while hopping up and down.

examples.ko: 참새가 깡충 하고 옆으로 뛰어서 자리를 옮겼어요.
examples.en: The sparrow gave a little hop sideways and moved its spot.

explain: 토끼나 아이처럼 작고 가벼운 것이 뛰는 모습에 어울려요. 크고 다리가 긴 느낌이면 '껑충'을 쓰고, '깡충깡충'처럼 반복해서도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It suits small, light things such as rabbits or children hopping. For something bigger with long legs, use '껑충'; the repeated form '깡충깡충' is also very common.

examples.en: The kids smashed the sandcastle with their feet.
It isn't easy to smash prejudice.

examples.ko: 동생이 블록으로 쌓은 탑을 깨부수고 웃었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling smashed the tower built of blocks and laughed.

examples.ko: 우리 선수가 세계 기록을 깨부수고 우승했어요.
examples.en: Our athlete smashed the world record and won.

examples.ko: 화가 나도 물건을 깨부수면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Even when you're angry, you must not smash things.

examples.ko: 낡은 벽을 깨부숴야 새로 지을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to tear down the old wall before you can build a new one.

explain: '부수다'보다 힘을 세게 줘서 때려 부수는 느낌이 있어요. '편견·기록·틀을 깨부수다'처럼 비유로도 자주 써요. 활용은 '깨부숴요, 깨부쉈어요'예요.
explain_en: It feels more forceful than '부수다', like smashing something with strength. It is also often used figuratively, as in breaking prejudice, records or molds. The conjugation is '깨부숴요, 깨부쉈어요'.

examples.en: The child learned to read Hangeul at the age of four.

examples.ko: 글을 깨치면 책 읽는 재미를 알게 돼요.
examples.en: Once you learn to read, you discover the fun of reading books.

examples.ko: 혼자 공부하면서 영어 원리를 깨치게 됐어요.
examples.en: Studying on my own, I came to grasp how English works.

examples.ko: 한글을 깨치지 못한 어른들을 위한 수업이에요.
examples.en: It's a class for adults who haven't learned Hangeul.
My grandmother learned to read late in life.
Once I grasped the principle, the problems became easy.

explain: '한글을 깨치다'처럼 글이나 원리를 익혀서 알게 될 때 자주 써요. '깨닫다'는 어떤 사실을 갑자기 알아차리는 느낌이 강하고, '깨치다'는 공부해서 알게 되는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is often used as in '한글을 깨치다', for coming to know a script or principle by learning it. '깨닫다' feels like suddenly realizing something, while '깨치다' feels like coming to understand through study.

examples.ko: 밤에 혼자 걷는 길은 왠지 꺼려져요.
examples.en: For some reason I feel reluctant about walking that road alone at night.

examples.ko: 친한 친구에게 돈 이야기를 하기가 꺼려져서 말을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I felt reluctant to talk about money with a close friend, so I couldn't say it.
It's raining hard, so I don't feel like going out.

examples.ko: 처음 보는 음식이라 먹기가 좀 꺼려졌어요.
examples.en: It was a food I'd never seen, so I felt a bit hesitant to eat it.

examples.ko: 그 사람과 단둘이 만나는 건 꺼려지는 일이에요.
examples.en: Meeting that person one-on-one is something I feel reluctant about.

examples.ko: 전에 사고가 난 뒤로 운전이 꺼려지더라고요.
examples.en: Since the accident before, I've felt reluctant to drive.

explain: 내가 일부러 피하는 '꺼리다'와 달리, 저절로 마음이 내키지 않는 느낌이에요. 보통 '-기가 꺼려지다', '○○이/가 꺼려지다'로 써요.
explain_en: Unlike '꺼리다', where you deliberately avoid something, this describes a reluctance that comes over you on its own. It is usually used as '-기가 꺼려지다' or '○○이/가 꺼려지다'.

examples.ko: 아이가 길에 있는 웅덩이를 껑충 뛰어넘었어요.
examples.en: The child leaped over the puddle in the road.
The puppy sprang over the fence and ran away.
Vegetable prices have jumped a lot lately.

examples.ko: 우리 아들이 한 해 만에 키가 껑충 컸어요.
examples.en: My son shot up in height in just one year.
My score jumped up a lot on this exam.
The deer bounded into the forest.

explain: '깡충'보다 크고 다리가 긴 것이 뛰는 느낌이에요. 물가·점수·키가 갑자기 많이 오를 때도 '껑충 뛰다, 껑충 오르다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It feels bigger than '깡충', like a long-legged animal leaping. It is also used when prices, scores or height rise suddenly, as in '껑충 뛰다' or '껑충 오르다'.

examples.en: At dawn, a rooster crowed cock-a-doodle-doo.
Every morning I wake up to the sound of crowing.

examples.ko: 아이가 닭 흉내를 내며 꼬끼오 하고 외쳤어요.
examples.en: The child imitated a rooster and shouted cock-a-doodle-doo.
In the storybook, there's a rooster that crows 'kkokkio!'

examples.ko: 시골 할머니 댁에서는 꼬끼오 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: At my grandmother's house in the countryside, you can hear crowing.
In Korean, a rooster's crow is called kkokkio.

explain: 수탉이 우는 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요. 영어의 cock-a-doodle-doo처럼 나라마다 소리 표현이 달라요. 병아리는 '삐악삐악', 암탉은 '꼬꼬댁'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It imitates a rooster's crow, and just like English cock-a-doodle-doo, each language writes this sound differently. Chicks say '삐악삐악' and hens say '꼬꼬댁'.

examples.en: I skipped lunch, so my stomach is growling.
My stomach growled in the quiet classroom and I was embarrassed.

examples.ko: 배가 꼬르륵거리는 소리가 옆 사람한테 들렸어요.
examples.en: The person next to me heard my stomach growling.

examples.ko: 아침부터 굶었는지 아이 배가 계속 꼬르륵거렸어요.
examples.en: The child's stomach kept rumbling, maybe from not eating since morning.

examples.ko: 배가 꼬르륵거릴 때는 간단히 뭐라도 먹어요.
examples.en: When your stomach is growling, eat something light.

examples.ko: 시험 시간에 배가 꼬르륵거리지 않게 아침을 먹고 왔어요.
examples.en: I ate breakfast so my stomach wouldn't growl during the exam.

explain: 주로 '배가'와 함께 써서 배고플 때 나는 소리를 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '배에서 꼬르륵 소리가 나요'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used with '배가' for the sound your stomach makes when hungry. People also commonly say '배에서 꼬르륵 소리가 나요' with the same meaning.

examples.en: How about oxtail soup for lunch today?
Oxtail soup has to simmer a long time for the broth to get rich.

examples.ko: 감기 기운이 있어서 따뜻한 꼬리곰탕을 먹었어요.
examples.en: I felt a cold coming on, so I had warm oxtail soup.

examples.ko: 이 집 꼬리곰탕에는 고기가 푸짐하게 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This place's oxtail soup has a generous amount of meat.
I put rice in the oxtail soup and had kkakdugi on the side.
My mother makes oxtail soup for us every weekend.

explain: 소꼬리를 오래 푹 고아서 만든 국이에요. 설렁탕, 갈비탕처럼 국물 요리 메뉴판에서 자주 만나고, 보통 소금과 파를 넣어 먹고 김치나 깍두기를 같이 먹어요.
explain_en: It is a soup made by simmering oxtail for a long time. You often see it on menus alongside seolleongtang and galbitang, and people usually season it with salt and green onion and eat it with kimchi or kkakdugi.

examples.en: I fell on the icy road and hurt my tailbone.

examples.ko: 꼬리뼈가 아파서 오래 앉아 있기 힘들어요.
examples.en: My tailbone hurts, so it's hard to sit for long.

examples.ko: 의자에 앉을 때 꼬리뼈가 눌려서 쿠션을 깔았어요.
examples.en: My tailbone got pressed when I sat, so I put a cushion down.
I landed hard on my bottom, and now my tailbone throbs.

examples.ko: 병원에서 꼬리뼈 사진을 찍어 보자고 했어요.
examples.en: At the hospital they said let's take an X-ray of the tailbone.
Humans have a tailbone, but no tail.

explain: 넘어져서 엉덩이를 세게 다쳤을 때 '꼬리뼈가 아프다'라고 구체적으로 말해요. 병원에서도 이렇게 설명하면 잘 통해요.
explain_en: When you fall and hurt your bottom, people say specifically '꼬리뼈가 아프다'. Describing it this way also works well at a hospital.

examples.en: I boiled cockles and dipped them in seasoned sauce.
Cockles are in season in winter, so they taste great.
I ordered cockle bibimbap and it was really delicious.
Cockles have ridges on their shells.
I bought a bag of cockles at the market.
Wash the cockles well and let them spit out sand first.

explain: 삶아서 양념에 무쳐 먹는 '꼬막무침'이나 '꼬막비빔밥'으로 많이 만나요. 그냥 '조개'라고 해도 되지만 꼬막은 메뉴 이름에서 따로 구별해서 불러요.
explain_en: You mostly meet it as seasoned boiled cockles (꼬막무침) or cockle bibimbap. You could just say '조개', but on menus cockles are named separately.

examples.en: The mountain road is winding, so please go slowly.
The baby's hair is curly.
If you follow the winding alley, you'll find a cafe.
The ramen noodles are curled up in squiggles.
The road isn't winding, so it's easy to drive.
The child drew a squiggly line on the paper.

explain: '구불구불'과 비슷해서 길, 머리카락, 선에 다 쓸 수 있어요. '꼬불꼬불'은 작게 여러 번 꺾이는 느낌으로 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is similar to '구불구불' and can describe roads, hair or lines. '꼬불꼬불' often gives the feeling of many small bends.

examples.en: I threaded the meat on a skewer and grilled it.

examples.ko: 꼬챙이로 찔러 보면 다 익었는지 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you poke it with a skewer, you can tell whether it's cooked through.
All you need is one thin skewer.
Grandmother threaded persimmons on a skewer to dry them.
The skewer is sharp, so be careful.
The skewer broke, so I bought a new one.

explain: 음식을 꿰는 막대 자체를 말하고, 꿴 음식은 보통 '꼬치'라고 해요. 막대나 쇠붙이처럼 가늘고 뾰족한 물건에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I haven't had an appetite lately and have become thin as a rail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 아주 가늘고 말랐다는 뜻이에요. 걱정하거나 놀랄 때 쓰고, 칭찬으로는 잘 안 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means extremely skinny. It is used when worried or surprised, and rarely as a compliment.

explain_en: It refers to the stick itself, while the skewered food is usually called '꼬치'. It can also be used for other thin, pointed sticks or metal pieces.

examples.en: I bought and ate grilled skewers on my way home from work.
I like chicken skewers best.
The smell of grilled skewers drifted from the night market.
I brushed sauce on the skewers and grilled them over charcoal.

examples.ko: 주말에 캠핑장에서 꼬치구이를 해 먹기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to make grilled skewers at the campsite this weekend.
This shop has a wide variety of grilled skewers.

explain: 고기나 채소를 꼬치에 꿰어 구운 음식이에요. 줄여서 그냥 '꼬치'라고도 많이 하고, '닭꼬치'처럼 재료 이름을 붙여 메뉴로 써요.
explain_en: It is food grilled on a skewer, such as meat or vegetables. People often shorten it to just '꼬치', and menus add the ingredient, as in '닭꼬치'.

examples.en: I got up before dawn and went to the airport.
Yesterday I couldn't fall asleep until the wee hours.

examples.ko: 꼭두새벽부터 공사 소리 때문에 잠이 깼어요.
examples.en: The construction noise woke me up before the crack of dawn.
How could you call at this hour? It's the middle of the night!
My father goes to the market before dawn.

examples.ko: 꼭두새벽에 출발했더니 길이 하나도 안 막혔어요.
examples.en: We left at the crack of dawn, so there was no traffic at all.

explain: '새벽'보다 훨씬 이른 시간이라는 점을 강조할 때 써요. 놀라거나 불평하는 말투에 자주 어울리고, 보통 '꼭두새벽에'로 말해요.
explain_en: It emphasizes that the time is much earlier than ordinary '새벽'. It often goes with a surprised or complaining tone, and is usually said as '꼭두새벽에'.

examples.en: A triangle has three vertices.
Connect the vertices of the square with lines.

examples.ko: 이 도형의 꼭짓점은 모두 몇 개예요?
examples.en: How many vertices does this shape have in total?

examples.ko: 꼭짓점에 A, B, C라고 이름을 붙였어요.
examples.en: I labeled the vertices A, B and C.
I counted the number of vertices of the solid shape.
Fold the paper and line up the corners with each other.

explain: 수학 시간에 도형의 선(변)이 만나는 점을 말할 때 써요. 도형 이야기에서는 '변'과 짝으로 같이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고 수업이나 교과서에서 많이 들려요.
explain_en: It is used in math class for the point where the lines (변) of a shape meet, and it often appears together with '변'. It is rare in daily conversation and mostly heard in lessons and textbooks.

en: being at a standstill; not budging

examples.ko: 눈길에서 차가 멈춰 버려서 두 시간 동안 꼼짝없이 기다렸어요.
examples.en: The car stopped on the snowy road, so I waited without moving for two hours.

examples.ko: 마감이 내일인데 일이 산더미라서 오늘 밤은 꼼짝없이 야근이에요.
examples.en: The deadline is tomorrow and the work is piled high, so tonight I'm stuck working overtime.

examples.ko: 문이 잠겨서 꼼짝없이 밖에서 떨어야 했어요.
examples.en: The door was locked, so I had no choice but to shiver outside.
This time there's evidence, so there's no way out for him.

examples.ko: 감기에 걸려서 이틀 동안 꼼짝없이 누워 있었어요.
examples.en: I caught a cold and lay in bed without budging for two days.

examples.ko: 이대로 가면 꼼짝없는 신세가 될 것 같아요.
examples.en: If this keeps up, I think I'll end up with no way out.

explain: 거의 '꼼짝없이'의 형태로 쓰고, 어쩔 수 없이 그 상태로 있어야 하는 상황에 어울려요. '꼼짝 못 하다'와 비슷하게 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is almost always used in the form '꼼짝없이', for situations where you have no choice but to stay that way. It is often used much like '꼼짝 못 하다'.

examples.en: Even though Grandfather is old, his back is still straight.

examples.ko: 아기가 벽을 잡고 꼿꼿이 서서 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: The baby is standing upright holding the wall, smiling.
Her posture is upright like a model's, so she stands out.
I sat up straight during the interview.

examples.ko: 그분은 끝까지 꼿꼿하게 자기 뜻을 지켰어요.
examples.en: He firmly held to his own will to the end.

examples.ko: 허리가 꼿꼿하지 않아서 거울을 자주 봐요.
examples.en: My back isn't straight, so I check the mirror often.

explain: 몸이나 막대가 구부러지지 않고 곧을 때 써요. 사람의 태도에 쓰면 굽히지 않고 당당하다는 뜻인데, 때로는 좀 뻣뻣하다는 느낌도 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a body or stick that does not bend. For a person's attitude it means firm and unyielding, though it can sometimes sound a little stiff.

examples.en: Every weekend I do flower arranging at the culture center.
My mother likes arranging flowers in the living room.
After arranging the flowers, the room became brighter.

examples.ko: 꽃꽂이한 화병을 식탁 위에 올려 놓았어요.
examples.en: I put the vase of arranged flowers on the dining table.
I bought a bunch of roses to arrange.

examples.ko: 이번 주말에 친구랑 같이 꽃꽂이해 볼래요?
examples.en: Do you want to try flower arranging with a friend this weekend?

explain: '꽃꽂이'는 취미나 수업 이름으로 많이 쓰고, '꽃꽂이를 배우다'처럼도 말해요. 동사로는 '꽃꽂이하다'를 쓰지만 '꽃을 꽂다'도 같은 상황에 가끔 써요.
explain_en: '꽃꽂이' is commonly used as the name of a hobby or class, as in '꽃꽂이를 배우다'. As a verb you use '꽃꽂이하다', and '꽃을 꽂다' is sometimes used in the same situation.

examples.en: Buds have started to form on the cherry tree.

examples.ko: 며칠 지나면 꽃봉오리가 활짝 필 거예요.
examples.en: In a few days the buds will bloom fully.
It's still a bud, so it's fine to put it in a vase.
I carefully touched the rose bud.

examples.ko: 봄비가 내린 뒤 꽃봉오리가 통통하게 부풀었어요.
examples.en: After the spring rain, the buds swelled up plump.
One flower bud burst open this morning.

explain: 활짝 핀 꽃은 '만개한 꽃', 아직 닫힌 상태는 '꽃봉오리'라고 구별해요. '봉오리'로 줄여 말하기도 하고, 앞날이 기대되는 어린 사람을 '꽃봉오리'에 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: A fully open flower is 만개한 꽃, while one still closed is a 꽃봉오리. It is also shortened to '봉오리', and a promising young person is sometimes compared to a 꽃봉오리.

examples.en: I fed the spotted deer at the park.
Spotted deer have white spots on their backs.
The spotted deer at the zoo had impressive antlers.

examples.ko: 꽃사슴이 숲속에서 조용히 풀을 뜯고 있어요.
examples.en: A spotted deer is quietly grazing in the forest.
The children shouted excitedly when they saw the spotted deer.
I read a picture book with a spotted deer and a rabbit.

explain: 그냥 '사슴'이라고 해도 되지만, 등에 흰 점무늬가 있는 사슴을 콕 집어 말할 때 써요. 동물원이나 공원 이야기에서 만날 수 있어요.
explain_en: You can simply say '사슴', but this word points specifically to deer with white spots on their backs. You may meet it in talk about zoos or parks.

examples.ko: 화분에 흙을 담을 때 꽃삽을 썼어요.
examples.en: I used a trowel to put soil into the flowerpot.
I dug the ground with a trowel and planted the seedlings.

examples.ko: 베란다 텃밭에는 작은 꽃삽이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There's a small trowel in the veranda garden.

examples.ko: 꽃삽 없이 맨손으로 흙을 팠더니 손이 아파요.
examples.en: I dug the soil with bare hands without a trowel and now my hands hurt.

examples.ko: 아이 생일 선물로 장난감 꽃삽을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a toy trowel as a birthday present for my child.

examples.ko: 꽃삽은 크기가 작아서 분갈이할 때 편해요.
examples.en: A trowel is small, so it's handy when repotting.

explain: 화분이나 작은 텃밭에서 흙을 팔 때 쓰는 작은 삽이에요. 땅을 크게 팔 때 쓰는 일반 '삽'과는 크기가 달라요.
explain_en: It is a small shovel for digging soil in flowerpots or small garden plots. It differs in size from the ordinary '삽' used for digging large areas.

examples.ko: 시장에서 갓 튀긴 꽈배기를 사 먹었어요.
examples.en: I bought and ate a freshly fried twisted doughnut at the market.
Twisted doughnuts taste even better coated with sugar.
I ordered a twisted doughnut and coffee as a snack.
I braided my hair into a twisted shape.

examples.ko: 이 집 꽈배기는 겉이 바삭하고 속이 쫄깃해요.
examples.en: This place's twisted doughnuts are crispy outside and chewy inside.

examples.ko: 꽈배기처럼 꼬인 줄을 푸느라 한참 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a long time to untangle the rope twisted like a pretzel.

explain: 밀가루 반죽을 길게 꼬아서 튀긴 간식이에요. 무언가가 심하게 꼬인 모양을 말할 때 '꽈배기처럼'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a snack made of dough twisted into a long shape and fried. People also say '꽈배기처럼' when describing something badly twisted.

examples.ko: 누가 문을 꽝꽝 두드려서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Someone banged on the door and I was startled.

examples.ko: 한강이 꽝꽝 얼어서 사람들이 구경하러 왔어요.
examples.en: The Han River froze solid, and people came to see it.

examples.ko: 아이가 화가 나서 방문을 꽝꽝 닫았어요.
examples.en: The child got angry and slammed the bedroom door again and again.

examples.ko: 냉동실에 넣어 둔 고기가 꽝꽝 얼었어요.
examples.en: The meat I put in the freezer has frozen solid.

examples.ko: 망치로 못을 꽝꽝 박는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear the sound of nails being hammered in with loud bangs.

examples.ko: 날이 추워서 물통이 꽝꽝 얼어 버렸어요.
examples.en: It's so cold that the water bottle froze solid.

explain: 세게 두드리거나 닫는 소리와, 아주 단단하게 언 상태를 말할 때 둘 다 써요. 얼음은 '꽝꽝 얼다'로 자주 붙여 쓰고, 소리는 '쾅쾅'도 같이 써요.
explain_en: It describes both loud banging sounds and something frozen very hard. Ice is often said as '꽝꽝 얼다', and for the sound '쾅쾅' is also used.

examples.en: I didn't want to do my homework, so I pretended to be sick.

examples.ko: 꾀병인 줄 알았는데 진짜 열이 있었어요.
examples.en: I thought he was faking it, but he really had a fever.

examples.ko: 동생이 학교에 안 가려고 꾀병을 부리는 것 같아요.
examples.en: My younger sibling seems to be faking illness to skip school.

examples.ko: 꾀병 부리지 말고 어서 일어나서 준비해요.
examples.en: Stop faking being sick and get up and get ready.
Mom quickly figured out that I was faking.

examples.ko: 시험 날만 되면 배가 아프다니 꾀병 아니에요?
examples.en: Your stomach only hurts on exam days? Aren't you faking it?

explain: 보통 '꾀병을 부리다'로 말해요. 진짜 아픈 사람에게 '꾀병이야'라고 하면 크게 실례가 되니 조심하세요.
explain_en: It is usually said as '꾀병을 부리다'. Be careful: telling someone who is truly sick '꾀병이야' is very rude.

examples.en: We're late, so don't dawdle, let's head out quickly.
A caterpillar is wriggling on the leaf.
Every morning I dawdle in bed and end up being late.
If you dawdle like that, you'll miss the train.
There's no time to dawdle, so hurry up.
The child dawdled for a long time while changing clothes.

explain: 벌레처럼 느리게 꿈틀대는 움직임에도 쓰지만, 일상에서는 행동이 느려서 재촉할 때 '꾸물거리지 마'라고 많이 말해요. 약간 답답해하는 말투가 있어서 윗사람에게는 조심해서 써요.
explain_en: It can describe slow wriggling like a worm's, but in daily life it is mostly used to urge someone on, as in '꾸물거리지 마'. It carries a slightly impatient tone, so be careful using it toward elders.

examples.en: People like her natural manner, so she has many friends.
Please tell me honestly, just as it is.
I put a lot of thought into decorating my room.

examples.ko: 꾸밈이 많은 글보다 간단한 글이 읽기 편해요.
examples.en: Simple writing is easier to read than ornate writing.
We learned about modifiers in Korean class.
The kids decorated the cake themselves.

explain: 일상에서는 '꾸밈없다'(솔직하고 자연스럽다)로 가장 많이 만나요. 동사 '꾸미다'와 짝이고, 국어 시간에는 '꾸밈말'이라는 말도 나와요.
explain_en: In daily life you meet it most often in '꾸밈없다' (natural and honest). It pairs with the verb '꾸미다', and in Korean class you also see the word '꾸밈말' (modifier).

examples.en: I bowed to the teacher and went into the classroom.
I nodded off on the bus and missed my stop.

examples.ko: 아이가 고개를 꾸벅 숙이며 고맙다고 했어요.
examples.en: The child bowed their head and said thank you.

examples.ko: 점심 먹고 나면 자꾸 꾸벅꾸벅 졸려요.
examples.en: After lunch I keep getting drowsy and nodding off.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 만날 때마다 꾸벅 인사해요.
examples.en: That person gives a quick bow every time we meet.

examples.ko: 꾸벅 절을 하고 나서야 어머니가 웃으셨어요.
examples.en: Only after I made a deep bow did Mother smile.

explain: 고개를 한 번 숙이는 인사에는 '꾸벅', 졸면서 고개가 계속 떨어지는 모습에는 '꾸벅꾸벅'을 써요. '꾸벅 인사하다', '꾸벅꾸벅 졸다'가 자주 붙는 짝이에요.
explain_en: Use '꾸벅' for a single quick bow of the head, and '꾸벅꾸벅' for the head repeatedly dropping while dozing off. '꾸벅 인사하다' and '꾸벅꾸벅 졸다' are common pairings.
